clue.text: Vestment needed by some duke

parts.note: an alb is a long white vestment worn by clergy
some, as in 'some person', means any

explanation.surface: A priest's robe is required by an aristocrat of unspecified rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' is the definition by example: the Duke of Albany is a royal title, so the answer is a dukedom standing for its holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Albany is a royal dukedom, so the holder of that title is a duke by example.

clue.text: In private, what every actor wants?

explanation.surface: Actors privately long for a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart can mean aside or privately; read as two words it is a role, which every performer craves.

clue.text: Give ground — go over area of financial planning

parts.note: to budge is to yield or move

indicators.note: over means the word for go is spread over the abbreviation for area

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Yield, then cover the district again as part of the money plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ground' reads as a concession in an argument; 'over' is the container signal here, wrapping the attempt around the area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgetary describes anything concerning a budget, an organisation's plan for spending money.

clue.text: Submariner's warning to change direction

indicators.note: to change direction means the word for warning is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: A submarine officer warns his crew to turn about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change direction' turns OMEN backwards. Captain Nemo is Jules Verne's submarine captain in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel, a famous undersea sailor.

clue.text: A ballet held very difficult at first — not for a beginner

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held means the word for ballet keeps the next piece inside it

parts.note: ballet is a kind of dance

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word difficult is used

explanation.surface: A ballet routine that was very hard from the start is no place for a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts V inside DANCE to make DVANCE; 'at first' takes the D of 'difficult' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced material is pitched above the level of someone just starting out, so it is not for novices.

clue.text: One short of cash feels this drink needed

definitions.text: One short of cash feels this

explanation.surface: Someone who is broke needs a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'feel the draught' is a British idiom for suffering from lack of money; 'needed' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel the draught is an idiom for being hard up; a draught is also a swallow of beer.

clue.text: Wren maybe giving a third off, go mad for piece of classical temple

indicators.note: giving a third off means the last third of the word for Wren's profession is removed

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren, designer of St Paul's Cathedral, was an architect
to rave is to rant wildly

explanation.surface: Wren loses a third of his work and goes berserk over part of an ancient shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving a third off' cuts the final three letters ECT from the nine-letter ARCHITECT, leaving ARCHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the beam resting directly on the column capitals in classical buildings.

clue.text: Poet, conspirator and wicked type, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word for wicked type is heard in a way that gives the answer

parts.note: a sinner is a wicked person

explanation.surface: A versifier, a plotter and a villain, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar there are two Cinnas: Cinna the poet and Cinna the conspirator. 'some say' asks for a non-rhotic pronunciation of SINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a poet and a plotter against Caesar bore this Roman name in history and in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Maximum effort of ladies to secure man over time

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the earlier pieces sit above the next one
to secure means the word for ladies holds the word for man inside it

parts.note: dames are ladies
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: Women try their hardest to keep a man for a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' is the container signal; 'over' works because in a down entry the earlier part sits on top of the time letter. To do one's damnedest is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's damnedest is an idiom for trying as hard as possible.

clue.text: Leaves two at bridge to enter water

parts.note: E and N, East and North, are two of the four players at bridge
to dive is to plunge into water

explanation.surface: Two card players leave the table to plunge into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the definition: endive is a salad plant eaten for its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a salad vegetable whose curly foliage is what is eaten.

clue.text: In bed, moan horribly, clutching this?

definitions.text: In bed, moan horribly, clutching this?

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of bed and moan are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed groaning and holding their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges the seven letters of BED and MOAN; the whole clue then pictures a sufferer with stomach ache clutching their belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone groaning in bed with a stomach complaint would hold their belly, the part of the body below the chest.

clue.text: A Catholic union concealing a mystery

indicators.note: concealing means the letters before it hide the following letter within them

parts.note: taken as written
RC stands for Roman Catholic
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Catholic marriage hides some secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like marriage in the surface but is the British miners' trade union; 'concealing' hides the second 'a' inside the whole run before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcanum is a secret or mysterious thing known only to initiates, a synonym for a mystery.

clue.text: Supporter's millions rain down

parts.note: a tee is a peg that supports a golf ball
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A backer's fortune comes pouring down on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wealthy backer, but the supporter is a golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to pour heavily, as rain does when it pelts down.

clue.text: Painful period getting to place one enters, making this?

definitions.text: Painful period getting to place one enters, making this?

indicators.note: getting to means the following pieces are placed after the earlier ones
enters means the word for one goes into the abbreviation for place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
I is the Roman numeral for one
painful means grim
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A hard spell of travel before reaching a holy site is the journey being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal and 'getting to' sets the order; the whole clue also describes a hard trek to a sacred place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a long, often arduous journey to a sacred shrine, which the clue's whole picture describes.

clue.text: Unable to get agreement precisely secured

parts.note: dead means exactly, as in dead centre
locked means secured

explanation.surface: Talks reach a point where everything is shut fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Negotiations that are deadlocked have reached a standstill with neither side giving way.

clue.text: Briefly organise binder for getting a job

indicators.note: briefly means the word for organise is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to organise something is to plan it
cement binds bricks together

explanation.surface: Set up some kind of glue quickly to get hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' is the deletion signal, cutting off the final letter; 'binder' reads as a folder in the surface but is the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is the act of finding someone a post, or the post itself, as with a work placement.

clue.text: Check on walker — safe, but clutching head

indicators.note: clutching means the word for safe holds the word for head inside it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
dome is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A hiker is examined: unharmed, but holding their head.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER as a safe is old thieves' slang, as in a peterman (safe-cracker). 'safe' reads as unhurt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts the steps of someone on foot, so it monitors a walker.

clue.text: Game needs one coin, say, or another

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: say means the coin's abbreviation is spelt as it is pronounced

parts.note: P is one penny, a British coin

explanation.surface: A sport requires a single coin, or maybe a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns P, one penny, into how it is spoken, PEE. Then 'another' is the definition: the rupee is a different coin, used in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India and Pakistan, so a further coin beside the penny.

clue.text: Long drink includes very soft fruit

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: includes means the word for drink holds the letters for very soft

parts.note: ale is a drink
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall drink contains some squishy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as tall but is the verb to yearn; 'includes' is the container signal, and pp is the musical marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a large tropical fruit with spiky skin.

clue.text: Spirit in the wood not sweet, notice

parts.note: dry wine is not sweet
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A forest ghost wine is not sugary, look.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a nymph inhabiting trees, a woodland sprite.

clue.text: Joiner in meeting-place finishing early in bad weather

indicators.note: in means the cut-short meeting place sits inside the word for bad weather

parts.note: sleet is unpleasant wintry weather

indicators.note: finishing early means the word for meeting-place loses its last letter

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: A carpenter in the meeting hall leaves early because of the storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter but is a fastener; 'finishing early' trims the last letter and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve nut is a threaded tube used to join two rods, a fastener that connects parts.

clue.text: Peak receiving precipitation (not English)

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is removed

parts.note: something snowed on has received snow

explanation.surface: A summit gets snow, though not in England.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOWDON is the highest mountain in Wales, which fits the surface's 'not English'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is a mountain in north Wales, the highest summit there.

clue.text: Prophet and priest, taking up 13

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

indicators.note: taking up means in a down clue the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is a holy journey, which Muslims call the hajj or haj

explanation.surface: A seer and a cleric take on a holy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses HAJ, the pilgrimage to Mecca, giving JAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is an Old Testament prophet who challenged the priests of Baal.

clue.text: More plots I develop in population centre

indicators.note: develop means the letters of the preceding words are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Further schemes are drawn up in a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' rearranges MORE PLOTS I; 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a major city, a large centre of population.

clue.text: A possible fall of the pound sees the back of bears — bulls too

definitions.text: A possible fall of the pound
the back of bears — bulls too

explanation.surface: A sterling slump sees off bears and bulls on the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: A tossed pound coin lands heads or the other side; bears and bulls, stock-market types in the surface, are taken as animals with rear ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossed coins land heads or the reverse side; animals such as bears and bulls have rear appendages.

clue.text: Light beat has power

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An illuminating thrashing is strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device giving light, the word light naming such a source.

clue.text: As flower girl, rather like daddy?

explanation.surface: A flower girl at a wedding resembles her father.
explanation.walkthrough: Poppy is a girl's name; read as pop plus -y, it means something like pop, daddy.
explanation.definitionFit: The red poppy is a bloom, Poppy is a female name, and pop-like means resembling one's father.

clue.text: Stick head down a bit, disfigured by this?

definitions.text: Stick head down a bit, disfigured by this?

indicators.note: head down a bit means the opening letter of the word for stick is moved one place further along

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A teenager hangs their head, embarrassed by a spotty face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head down a bit' moves C, the first letter of CANE, one place lower in the down entry; the whole clue pictures a spotty adolescent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition of spots and pimples that can mark the face.

clue.text: Done right, getting appropriate mark outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for getting a tick goes round the letter for right

parts.note: work given a tick has been marked as correct, so it is ticked

explanation.surface: Correctly completed work is ticked by the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done' reads as finished but means cheated; 'outside' puts TICKED round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being done is slang for being cheated or deceived, the sense of being fooled.

clue.text: Lawman tucks into a chop and a drink

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tucks into means the word for lawman goes inside the following letters

parts.note: to lop is to chop off
a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman eats a pork chop and has something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but puts COP inside ALOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet fizzy beverage containing alcohol.

clue.text: Feel bad about one daughter, always in memory

indicators.note: about means the word for feeling bad goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to resent something is to feel bitter about it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A parent feels guilt about a daughter who is never forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ID inside RESENT. 'always in memory' is computing language: a program kept permanently loaded is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, a resident program stays permanently loaded in main memory.

clue.text: Let me show you why I say this view is unacceptable

parts.note: here's is what someone says when handing over or showing something

indicators.note: I say means the word why is replaced by a letter that is spoken the same way

parts.note: the word why is spoken exactly like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they consider an opinion intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' tells the solver that 'why' becomes the letter Y, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief contrary to accepted doctrine, an opinion the authorities refuse to tolerate.
